Reg. 1209)'; 41 CFR 60-300.2 and 61-300.2 (amended through 2026-10-26) repeat the reference; no revocation found by the bounded searches; checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1 establishes the Armed Forces Service Medal and states criterion (a): participation, on or after June 1, 1992 and in the Joint Chiefs of Staff's opinion, in a significant U.S. military operation with other Armed Force personnel. No held later instrument amends or ends it, and current 38 U.S.C. 4212 and the 2026 eCFR texts still refer to a service medal awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Same current references as section 1: 38 U.S.C. 4212 and 41 CFR 60-300.2 and 61-300.2 refer to the medal awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985; no revocation found; checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1(b) adds the second criterion for the medal: the member encounters no foreign armed opposition or imminent hostile action. No held instrument amends or ends it, and the medal it defines is still referred to in current law.

clauses.current_legal_basis: U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints Ex. Ord. No. 12985 under a note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13286, section 20; no later instrument found by the bounded searches; checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14 as amended. Section 2 provides that the medal is of a design approved by the Secretary of Defense and is awarded by the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation as to the Coast Guard when not operating in the Navy, with precedence immediately before the Humanitarian Service Medal. EO 13286 section 20, effective March 1, 2003, struck the words the Secretary of Transportation and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; the clause continues as amended under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21, and that substitution is recorded as a later event. The Code note prints the order 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13286, § 20'.

clauses.current_legal_basis: 38 U.S.C. 4212 and 41 CFR 60-300.2 and 61-300.2 still refer to the Armed Forces service medal awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985; the held later orders EO 13154 and EO 13289 describe the section as continuing for persons they do not cover; checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 3 limits award to operations for which no other U.S. service medal is approved, requires a lack of another suitable award where only one Military Department or the Coast Guard participates, and allows one medal per person with devices for later operations. EO 13154 section 2 (2000-05-03) and EO 13289 section 3 (2003-03-12) apply 'Notwithstanding section 3' to members who qualified for this medal by Kosovo service or by terrorism-related operations, keeping them qualified and allowing the Kosovo Campaign Medal or the Global War on Terrorism medals in lieu; those are exceptions recorded as later events, not ends, and the section continues for other operations.

clauses.current_legal_basis: U.S. Code release point 119-121 note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 prints Ex. Ord. No. 12985 with only the EO 13286 section 20 amendment listed; no revocation found; checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 4 allows the medal to be awarded posthumously and presented to a representative of the deceased as the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary of Transportation deems appropriate. No held instrument amends or ends it; EO 13286 section 20 changed only section 2. The Code note prints the order as amended by section 20 of EO 13286 only.

research_rationale:
EO 12985 (61 FR 1209, signed 1996-01-11, published 1996-01-18) establishes the Armed Forces Service Medal. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12985.txt): section 1 establishes the medal for members of the Armed Forces who on or after June 1, 1992 participate in a significant U.S. military operation and encounter no foreign armed opposition or imminent hostile action; section 2 provides for design approval and award by the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation (as to the Coast Guard when not operating in the Navy) and precedence before the Humanitarian Service Medal; section 3 limits award to operations for which no other U.S. service medal is approved and allows one medal with devices for later operations; section 4 allows posthumous award. The text has no sunset, deadline or condition. Later instruments found by reading the held texts that cite the number: EO 13286 section 20 (signed 2003-02-28, effective 2003-03-01 under its section 92) strikes the words the Secretary of Transportation in section 2 and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security in their place (the Code note records it as 'amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13286, § 20'); EO 13154 section 2 (2000-05-03) and EO 13289 section 3 (2003-03-12) each say 'Notwithstanding section 3 ... of Executive Order 12985' and let members who qualified for the Armed Forces Service Medal by Kosovo service or by terrorism-related operations remain qualified while also allowing the Kosovo Campaign Medal or the Global War on Terrorism medals in lieu of it. Those are exceptions and amendments, listed as later events on sections 2 and 3; none revokes or supersedes any clause. The dossier's EO 12977 record is not an event: its provision text is EO 13286 section 23, and EO 12977 (1995-10-19) predates this order. Current predicate: 38 U.S.C. 4212 (U.S. Code release point 119-121) still defines veterans by an 'Armed Forces service medal' awarded pursuant to Executive Order No. 12985; 41 CFR 60-300.2 and 61-300.2 (eCFR amended through 2026-10-26) carry the same reference; the Code also prints the order as a note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57. The bounded searches found no revocation. The text relied on is the held official Federal Register text; no transcription is used.
